We evaluate our proposed method on five translation tasks, i.e., WMT'14 EN $\leftrightarrow$ DE, WMT'16 EN $\leftrightarrow$ RO and IWSLT'14 DE $\rightarrow$ EN. Following previous works (Hinton et al., 2015; Kim and Rush, 2016; Gu et al., 2018; Zhou et al., 2020), we train a vanilla base transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) on each dataset and use its translations as the training data. The BLEU score (Papineni et al., 2002) is used to evaluate the translation quality. Latency, the average decoding time (ms) per sentence with batch size 1, is employed to measure the inference speed. All models' decoding speed is measured on a single NVIDIA Titan RTX GPU. We follow most of the hyperparameters for the CMLM (Ghazvininejad et al., 2019) in the base configuration, i.e., 6 layers for encoder and decoder, 8 attention heads, 512 embedding dimensions and 2048 hidden dimensions.
